info.title: CareerCraft
info.description:
Resume parsing, job matching and cover letter drafting — all local.

This API backs the CareerCraft web UI. The primary interface to the same
functionality is the MCP server (`careercraft-mcp`), which plugs into Claude
Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor.

`GET /api/capabilities` reports which optional features this install has;
anything unavailable comes with the command that enables it.

get.description:
Liveness, and enough about the install to be worth curling.

A health check that only says "ok" tells you nothing you did not already
know from the connection succeeding — but this is the one route without
AuthDep, so what it says has to be safe to say to a stranger. It reports
the install: version, and whether a model is reachable. It no longer
reports the store's row counts, which described the user.
Which optional features this install has, and how to enable the rest.

schema.title: Response Recent Jobs Api Jobs Recent Get
Response Saved Jobs Api Jobs Saved Get

post.description:
Accept an upload and parse it.

The client-supplied filename is discarded rather than sanitised — only its
extension survives — and the body is streamed to disk with the size cap
enforced as bytes arrive, so an oversized upload cannot fill the disk
before anyone checks.

Parse pasted resume text.

There is deliberately no ``path=`` equivalent here. Over HTTP the caller
is not necessarily the person running the server, and a tool that reads
server-side paths on request is a file-disclosure primitive.

Capabilities.title: Capabilities
Capabilities.description:
What this particular install can actually do.

Exposed as the ``careercraft://capabilities`` resource so a host model can
read it once and stop offering features that would only fail.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description:
Liveness. Deliberately free of anything about the user.

This used to carry ``stats`` — the row counts of every table — and it is
the one route with no ``AuthDep``, because a health check that requires a
credential is not much of a health check. That combination told any
unauthenticated caller how many resumes and letters the operator had
stored. Version and model availability describe the *install*, which is
already public at ``/capabilities``; row counts describe the *user*.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable content hash; the same posting always gets the same id.

Job.title: Job
Job.description: A single job posting, normalised across sources.

missing_skills.title: Missing Skills
missing_skills.description: Skills the posting emphasises that the resume does not mention.

LetterBrief.title: LetterBrief
LetterBrief.description:
What to say, when no language model is available to say it.

Returned instead of prose when Ollama is unreachable. The MCP host's own
model is generally *better* at writing the letter than a local 1B model —
it just needs the grounded material, which is what this is.

allow_brief.title: Allow Brief
allow_brief.description: The web UI has no model to hand a brief to, so it defaults to false and gets finished prose from the template instead.

LetterResponse.title: LetterResponse
LetterResponse.description: A generated letter plus the id it was stored under.

ParsedResume.title: ParsedResume
ParsedResume.description: The output of resume parsing, and the input to matching.

ResumeSummary.title: ResumeSummary
ResumeSummary.description: A row in ``list_resumes`` — enough to pick one, not the whole document.
